definitions.explanation: A rubber stamp or ink stamp used for marking documents, collecting at tourist spots, or as a children's toy.
An illustrated image or animated graphic sent in messaging apps like LINE. Larger and more expressive than emoji, stickers are a major feature of Japanese mobile communication.

examples.japanese: スタンプラリーに{参加|さんか}する。
examples.english: To participate in a stamp rally.

examples.japanese: {駅|えき}でスタンプを{集|あつ}めるのが{子|こ}どもの{頃|ころ}の{楽|たの}しみだった。
examples.english: Collecting stamps at train stations was one of my childhood pleasures.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しいスタンプを{買|か}った。
{返事|へんじ}に{困|こま}ったときはスタンプで{済|す}ませることが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: When I'm not sure how to reply, I often just send a sticker instead.

notes:
STAMP RALLY:
スタンプラリー is a popular activity in Japan where participants visit multiple locations (stations, tourist spots, shops) to collect stamps on a card. Completing all stamps often earns a prize.

LINE STICKERS:
LINE stickers (LINEスタンプ) are a distinctive feature of Japanese mobile culture. Users can purchase or download free sticker sets featuring characters, celebrities, or original designs. Sending stickers instead of text is very common in casual conversation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- スタンプを{押|お}す: to press/stamp a stamp
- スタンプラリー: stamp rally
- LINEスタンプ: LINE sticker
- スタンプを{送|おく}る: to send a sticker
